notes: §1985:X.5.2.4 GR9 states a requirement on the program: a CALL to a COBOL program carries USING 'only if there is a USING phrase in the Procedure Division header of the called program, in which case the number of operands in each USING phrase must be identical'; it gives no result for a violation, so §1985:I.1.6 ('The results of violating the formats or rules of Standard COBOL are undefined') applies and the compiler owes correct execution of matching calls only. CallBinder#BindCall binds the operands positionally, CallEmitter#InvocationText renders them as the CobolArg array, and ProgramTable#Activate lands them on the callee's formals; its count check is gated on EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH checking, which 85 cannot enable (>>TURN refused, COBOL0900), so a mismatch runs leniently, which the undefined result permits. Probes at --std 85: matching count with an ODO group, an 18-digit signed BY CONTENT and an edited item passed and returned correctly (G=4ABC, S unchanged); fewer, more and no arguments to a separately compiled and to a contained callee ran without a diagnostic (undefined); OMITTED, BY VALUE and an OPTIONAL formal were refused (COBOL0900, 2002+). The witness exercises two equal USING lists.

next.reason: 1985 requires 'the number of operands in each USING phrase must be identical' for a COBOL callee. 2023 reaches the count rule through §2023:14.9.4.3 SR25 and §2023:14.9.4.4 GR3 ('the rules for conformance specified in 14.8.2, Parameters ... apply'), and §2023:14.8.2.1 (uncatalogued prose) makes the counts equal 'with the exception of trailing formal parameters that are specified with an OPTIONAL phrase' and omitted; §2023:14.9.4.4 GR11 gives the omitted-argument condition for them. Looser: fewer arguments are allowed. A detected mismatch now sets EC-PROGRAM-ARG-MISMATCH when checking is enabled (§2023:14.9.4.4 GR3 d). The non-COBOL case stays implementor-defined (GR3 b, g). GR2 (positional correspondence) restates 1985 GR10, not this rule.
